reason: ASK-282. Arm the two .claude/ write-path guards. Layer 1 (claude-path-write-guard.py) blocks the ordinary Bash write shapes at PreToolUse. Layer 2 (claude-integrity-tripwire.py --enforce) is the real control: it ignores command shape and checks whether the CONTENT of .claude/ moved, so an unlisted command form is not an evasion. Both scripts, and their 41-case suite, landed on the ASK-282 branch. They CANNOT be wired by the agent that wrote them, because wiring means editing .claude/settings.json -- which is the exact vulnerability being closed. That is why this is a proposal and not a commit.

edits.reason: Layer 1. PreToolUse on Bash. Closes the measured hole: `touch .claude/_probe.txt` succeeded via Bash while Write/Edit were refused on the same path. The insert closes the existing Write|Edit|MultiEdit hooks array and opens a Bash sibling; the file's own following `]` and `}` close the new block, so the result stays valid JSON. Additive: no existing hook string is touched.

Layer 2, the control that actually holds. PostToolUse. This is the entry that narrows the detection window from one SESSION to one TOOL CALL. --enforce (not --check) is correct HERE and only here: on this path the actor is provably the agent, because the founder's own editor is not a tool call. Drift is quarantined before it is reverted, so a false positive costs nothing.

notes: SETTINGS-TEMPLATE PAIR REQUIRED BEFORE THIS APPLIES. settings-template-sync-check fails in both directions, so a matching pair of entries must be added to settings-template.json in the same proposal or the applier will (correctly) refuse. Those anchors were not transcribed here because they were not verified against the file byte-for-byte, and an unverified anchor is a guess. Verify both, then extend this proposal.
The anchors above were taken verbatim from .claude/settings.json at 1389d4c. If settings.json moved since, the applier refuses loudly with 'anchor not found' rather than applying to the wrong place.

Layer 2 is ALREADY ARMED at session granularity without this proposal, via q-system/hooks/session-start.py, which is wired and lives outside .claude/. This proposal only tightens the window; it is not what makes the tripwire exist.
